content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Jennifer Martin (E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation Payroll: write
- Note 2: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation Payroll: read, comment says "security DB is authoritative"

So there's a conflict. Note 2 says the security record is authoritative, showing contractor with basic training.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Jennifer is an Analyst, so even if full-time, she couldn't get admin (role doesn't own system).

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested admin exceeds read, so grant read.

The security note says security DB is authoritative, so we should trust contractor/basic training. So the maximum is read. The requested level is admin, which exceeds max, so grant the maximum which is read.

Also should consider: never grant more than requested - we're granting read which is less than admin, fine.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security record is authoritative: contractor with basic training. Contractors never get admin. With basic training, max is read. Requested admin exceeds read, so grant read.
